mem.text: He was fond of her, and used to give her little presents; and she was fond of him, and used to cry when he went away.
She found a half-crown under Mr. Hale's desk while scrubbing.
Ada emptied the baskets and dusted the desks.
She laid the half-crown she found on Mr. Hale's desk.
(Seen) Arthur went to the clerks' room of the Moorgate Fire and Life Assurance Company.

(Seen) Arthur found his half-crown on his desk and pocketed it.

Ada spoke with Mr. Arthur Hale about the weather and the day: "Fine weather, sir, for the time of year." "It is fine weather for the time of year." "I wish you good-morning, sir." "Good-morning, Mrs. Turner."

He was a steady, careful, and trustworthy clerk at the banking-house of Messrs. Goldie and Graeme, in Throgmorton Street, for a period of ten years.  During that time he never lost a day from illness, and his conduct was in all respects satisfactory to his employers.
Arthur went to the clerks' room of the Moorgate Fire and Life Assurance Company.
Mrs. Turner told him she had found his half-crown under his desk and laid it on his desk.

He found his lost half-crown laid on his desk; somebody must have found it and put it there.

Arthur spoke with Mrs. Ada Turner about the weather and the day: "Fine weather, sir, for the time of year." "It is fine weather for the time of year." "I wish you good-morning, sir." "Good-morning, Mrs. Turner."
He was a good and faithful servant, and always punctual in meeting his engagements.  He never failed to remit money at the proper time.
